input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the walk over exc.__cause__ has no cycle guard, so a chain that loops back on itself never reaches None
- failure path: an exception raised with `raise e from e`, or two exceptions that cause each other, makes retry_if_exception_cause_type spin forever at full CPU; the stop conditions never run and the caller hangs

Reviewer finding
- description: The cycle guard (`seen` set of visited exception ids) was removed from the `__cause__` traversal loop. A cyclic `__cause__` chain now makes the loop run forever.
- rationale: Trigger: an exception whose `__cause__` chain loops back, e.g. `a.__cause__ = b; b.__cause__ = a`, where neither cause matches `exception_cause_types`. The loop `while exc is not None` then never terminates, because `exc = exc.__cause__` just cycles. Impact: the retry predicate hangs at 100% CPU instead of returning False.
critique: The finding identifies the missing cycle guard in the __cause__ traversal. It also gives the same mechanism: a cyclic chain makes the loop spin forever at full CPU. This matches the labeled root cause and failure path.
